name: URL-backed related-view navigation with semantic separation
summary: For independent, related non-sequential destinations, links in a current-state navigation pattern may be more appropriate than in-place tab panels or stepper controls.
problem: The appearance of tabs obscures whether the user is navigating to distinct pages, revealing in-page panels, or progressing required steps.
context: Product section with related peer pages/views, each meaningful independently and addressable by its own URL.
observed_solution: Use linked related-view navigation with a current-page marker for URL-backed peers; reserve in-place tabs for content sections and step indicators for sequential task processes.
rationale: Primer UnderlineNav guidelines document URL-backed, non-sequential related views (O33) and pinned code renders current links/overflow (O37/O38); GOV.UK Tabs operates on related page sections and cautions against page navigation/linear processes (O21); GOV task-flow guidance O17.
tradeoffs: Page destinations may involve navigation transitions compared with in-place panels.
Many peer views need other nav structures rather than a crowded tab row.
User tasks requiring side-by-side comparison may not suit either tab model.
applicability: Separately addressable, sibling-like related destinations with no forced completion sequence.
accessibility_implications: Preserve descriptive link purpose and current-page state; never infer keyboard behavior from appearance; no AT validation.
performance_implications: No page load or rendering measurement; GOV explicitly warns of tabs page weight in some contexts.
responsive_implications: Overflowed peer destinations must remain available; pinned UnderlineNav implements a menu fallback but runtime untested.
implementation_notes: Do not impose ARIA tab panel roles on ordinary URL nav links.
No React/router selection is implied by observing Primer source.
A link-based related view need not use UnderlineNav specifically.

counterexamples.summary: GOV.UK Tabs supports switching self-contained content regions within a single page where separately navigable URLs are not required.
counterexamples.context: Brief related in-page sections for regular service users.
